metadata.channel_rule: gate = valid & ((area_cells >= a_min_cells) | (gate_q >= q_min for at least one declared, available, finite, nonnegative flux quantity)); a gate on a lower-bound quantity selects only cells whose known lower bound already passes, and the count of such cells is reported. The gate is a property selection, not a routability claim: routable channel = gate & (receiver >= 0), and gate & (receiver < 0) is kept separately as selected terminal anchors. Neither half is dropped.

clock.semantics: interval i owns [edges[i], edges[i+1]); every declared flux quantity shares this one clock

declared_gates.gate_policy: first-card configuration candidates, part of every reach identity; not frozen physical thresholds

metadata.display_line_policy: not_provided_in_v1: the ordered native trace is the authority; a simplified polyline may never be used for excavation, routing or physics and is not shipped here
metadata.downstream_rule: reach_downstream is the reach that owns the receiver target of this reach's tail cell, or -1 when the tail drains into its structural terminal; a downstream reach is never inferred across a root boundary

hydraulic_state.reason: no water depth, stage or hydraulic state is produced in this layer; a real routed event flux is physical water and is not a hydraulic state

metadata.local_q_policy: area is an upstream cell count and is never called discharge; flux is reported per declared quantity with its own completeness, and a missing local input is propagated downstream instead of being read as zero

source_model_scenario.missing_input_policy: a cell without local input is seeded unknown and propagated downstream; it is never read as zero

provenance.availability_policy: only cells the event model declares are available; every other valid cell of this support is unavailable and is propagated downstream as unknown, never read as zero
provenance.claimed_as: a declared event scenario on this support, not a climatology and not a hydraulic state

semantics.claim: a declared event model's real production routed on this support; this is physical water, and it is still not a hydraulic state

metadata.reach_identity_policy: reach_id = 'rb-' + sha256 over a world-anchored logical payload (algorithm, logical version, channel rule, both gates, world seed, spacing, plan_version, the root's world (x,z), the ordered source-to-tail world path digest and the downstream rule). The support origin/shape, local flat indices, reach_index and the selection of other reaches are excluded, so the same world reach keeps one id in a wider support; the path digest is over the ordered sequence and never over a set.
metadata.segmentation_rule: a reach starts at a channel cell whose channel-donor count is not 1 (0 = source, >= 2 = junction) and continues downstream while the next cell is a plain channel continuation; a junction cell belongs to the downstream reach, so reaches are maximal and vertex-disjoint; one-cell source and confluence reaches are kept
metadata.side_input_policy: a branch is resolved to one side-input slot; aggregated and refined are both computed and compared, and storing both would double count the same supply
